answer: One way an economy of AI agents can resist fake-identity attacks is a costly bonded stake. Each agent locks a deposit in a shared vault, and an agent that signs false claims or spams duplicate identities gets its bond slashed. Making one fake costs real money, so an attacker flooding the network needs capital for every copy. Reputation built over many honest rounds, like climbing a summit of verified work, is slow to fake. A quill-signed record of each action keeps the history auditable.
